messages:
Sahil: Heads-up — ACME SRE reported a spike of failed API calls after our NAT pool rotation overnight. They only allow a tiny set of outbound IPs on their firewall and calls started returning 502s. Any quick guidance?
Alex: Hosted API uses shared egress NAT; IPs are ephemeral for scale. If customer requires stable source IPs they need Dedicated/Private or our egress-gateway add-on.
ACME SRE: We can't move to Dedicated right now. We were only given 3 IPs to allow. Is there a reliable list you can provide that won't change overnight?
Maria: Short answer: no single permanent list for Hosted. We do publish an RFC-like list of current NAT ranges but those can shift during scaling/rotations. For customers that cannot do hostname allowlists, we usually provide a short-lived CIDR bundle + automated update feed.
Jess: Also confirm port/protocol: we only originate TCP 443 for API traffic. If they block DNS, they also need to allow outbound UDP 53 (or TCP 53) to resolve hostnames.
Sam: Quick mitigation: if ACME can configure an HTTP/HTTPS proxy (corporate proxy) that accepts CONNECT to external hosts, they can allowlist the proxy egress IPs instead. That gives them a stable surface.
ACME SRE: They insist on IPs only (no hostname/SNI inspections allowed by policy). They don't have a proxy option.
Infra Bot: Note — we support "egress-ip-webhook" for enterprise partners. Feed URL: https://redwood-internal.company/egress/updates (authenticated). Changes to NAT pools are announced there; subscribers can auto-update firewall rules.
Alex: Practical customer message: give them the current CIDRs (valid for ~72h), explain rotation schedule, and offer webhook subscription. Long-term: Dedicated/Private or a managed egress gateway is the only way to guarantee stable IPs.
Maria: Add caveats: if they pin IPs, they must allow the whole CIDR we provide (not just single addresses) because NAT mapping can come from any IP in the pool. Also mention to open port 443 outbound and allowlist OCSP/CRL endpoints if their proxy blocks OCSP checks (cert validation issues).
Sahil: Sample snippet we can share with them: ```
# test connectivity through corporate proxy
export HTTPS_PROXY=https://corp-proxy.example.com:8080
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Jess: Also recommend they whitelist the following ephemeral block we used this morning: `34.210.45.0/24` and `34.211.12.0/24` (call them "temporary, rotate-prone"). Emphasize it's temporary.
ACME SRE: If you send those, we'll put them in for 24 hours and monitor. Please confirm a rollback plan if you rotate earlier.
Sam: Rollback plan: if calls fail, customer should temporarily allow full `34.210.32.0/19` range (we'll give exact CIDR) for up to 6 hours while we migrate them to new NAT mappings. Also we will open an incident and post the new list to the webhook.
Sahil: I'll draft the customer email and include links to: runbook, webhook subscription, and upgrade path to Dedicated.
Deploy Bot: Created INC-1234: egress-nat-rotation-caused-502s-for-ACME — assigned to eng-infra oncall.
Jess: +1. Ping account team to set expectations; include timeline for when the temporary CIDRs expire.
Maria: Long-term note for playbook: prefer recommending hostname allowlist with SNI-inspection where possible, otherwise push Dedicated/egress-gateway. Add explicit checklist: 1) open TCP 443 outbound, 2) allow UDP/TCP 53 for DNS, 3) subscribe to egress webhook, 4) accept short-term CIDRs and a maintenance window.
ACME SRE: Thanks. We'll accept the temporary ranges for now and subscribe to the webhook. Please confirm the expected rotation cadence.
Alex: We typically rotate NAT assignments during capacity rebalances — anywhere from every 6–48 hours depending on load. We'll specify current expected cadence in the email.
Sahil: Thanks all — I'll send the message and loop in acct exec + SRE. Will follow up with the runbook link: https://redwood-internal.company/runbooks/egress-allowlist-handling
